clue.text: Plant associated with flag by Berger

definitions.meaning: a flowering shrub with scented purple or white blossom
John Berger's novel ... and Flag pairs this shrub with the flag in its title

explanation.definitionFit: The shrub is a common garden plant, and Berger's novel title Lilac and Flag links it with a flag.

clue.text: In which Bennett failed to score?

definitions.text: In which Bennett failed to score?

parts.words: In which Bennett failed to score
parts.note: Arnold Bennett wrote a play of this title; in tennis a game where one player wins no points is one in which the other failed to score

explanation.definitionFit: Tennis scoring calls zero 'love', so a contest with no points for one side earns this name, also a Bennett play title.

clue.text: Never Leave Well Enough Alone man starts looking over Englishman's weird yarn

definitions.text: Never Leave Well Enough Alone man

indicators.note: the starts of the five following words are their opening letters, taken in turn

explanation.surface: An autobiographer begins by casting an eye over an odd tale spun by an Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: Raymond Loewy, the industrial designer, called his autobiography Never Leave Well Enough Alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Raymond Loewy the designer wrote the memoir with that title, so he is its man.

clue.text: Hoffmann's Der Sandmann became a girl with enamel eyes

definitions.text: Hoffmann's Der Sandmann became a girl with enamel eyes

parts.words: Hoffmann's Der Sandmann became a girl with enamel eyes
parts.note: the Delibes ballet based on Hoffmann's tale centres on a mechanical doll with painted eyes

explanation.definitionFit: Delibes's ballet adapted Hoffmann's story, and its title role is the lifelike automaton girl.

clue.text: Flyer unfortunately shot by crew member

definitions.meaning: a large seabird, so something that flies
in Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner a sailor shoots the bird with his crossbow, bringing disaster

explanation.definitionFit: The great seabird is a flyer, and Coleridge's mariner kills one, bringing a curse on his ship.

clue.text: A Spanish hero may be vitriolic

parts.note: El Cid is the medieval Castilian warrior hero

explanation.surface: A Spanish champion may turn out to have a biting tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitriol is sulphuric acid, so vitriolic and the corrosive chemical are the same idea, also used of caustic speech.

clue.text: Superior work by 20

definitions.meaning: the upper class or finer kind of people
Henry James (20) published a story collection of this title

explanation.definitionFit: Finer folk are called the upper kind of people, and Henry James titled a 1903 story collection so.

clue.text: Corelli's girl observed in bethel, making her peace

indicators.note: the name can be seen sitting within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A girl in a chapel finds peace of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: Marie Corelli's 1887 novel is named after its Norwegian heroine; a bethel is a nonconformist chapel.
explanation.definitionFit: Corelli's novel takes its title from its heroine's name.

clue.text: Spy genre pioneer suggests a little work with writer on German home

parts.note: op is the short form of opus, a musical work
a pen is something that writes
Heim is the German word for home

explanation.surface: A thriller writer is said to have penned a short piece about a house in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: E. Phillips Oppenheim wrote dozens of early spy thrillers such as The Great Impersonation.
explanation.definitionFit: E. Phillips Oppenheim was among the first popular writers of espionage fiction.

clue.text: Daddy's girl showing some staying power

definitions.meaning: grit or resolve, as in nerves of a tough metal

explanation.definitionFit: Danielle Steel wrote Daddy, and the hard metal stands for toughness and endurance.

clue.text: Arthur Miller found one on a bridge

definitions.text: Arthur Miller found one on a bridge

parts.words: Arthur Miller found one on a bridge
parts.note: Miller's play A View from the Bridge suggests a spot offering a vantage

explanation.definitionFit: A vantage spot gives a view, and Miller's play takes its view from a bridge.

clue.text: Eliot's adopted child

parts.note: in George Eliot's Silas Marner the weaver takes in a golden-haired orphan

explanation.definitionFit: Silas Marner adopts the orphaned toddler who wanders into his cottage.

clue.text: Dennis Wheatley reported it in Greece

definitions.text: Dennis Wheatley reported it in Greece

parts.words: Dennis Wheatley reported it in Greece
parts.note: Wheatley wrote the thriller ... in Greece, so he told of chaos there

explanation.definitionFit: Wheatley's novel title names the chaos and violence found in Greece.

clue.text: Zola's embryonic work

parts.note: Zola's mining novel is named after a revolutionary month; the word also means budding or in seed

explanation.definitionFit: Zola's novel takes its title from a revolutionary calendar month, and the word means in the bud, like an embryo.

clue.text: Essential mood, though Kant's could be hypothetical

definitions.text: mood, though Kant's could be hypothetical
definitions.meaning: the grammatical mood of commands; Kant distinguished categorical and hypothetical kinds

explanation.definitionFit: Something vital is a must, the command mood in grammar, and Kant's moral command came categorical or hypothetical.

clue.text: Apostrophe to by 20?

parts.note: an apostrophe is an address to an absent figure, as to Melpomene; Henry James (20) wrote a novel with this title

explanation.walkthrough: The clue seems to have lost a word or two in printing; the reading rests on the James novel title.
explanation.definitionFit: Melpomene presides over drama of sorrow, and Henry James named an 1890 novel after her.

clue.text: Collins stories -not light reading?

definitions.meaning: Wilkie Collins published a collection of tales with this title
reading done when night has fallen, without daylight

explanation.definitionFit: Wilkie Collins titled an 1856 story collection so, and reading at night is done without daylight.

clue.text: King's zone

parts.note: Stephen King's novel The ... Zone

explanation.definitionFit: Stephen King's novel names the zone in its title, The Dead Zone.

clue.text: Douglas Reeman's Exterminator

parts.note: Reeman wrote naval fiction including a novel with this warship type as its title

explanation.definitionFit: One who exterminates wipes out, and the naval writer's novel title is also a fast warship.

clue.text: "What thin-s, cold affections" (Henry Vaughan, Silex Scirtillans)

definitions.text: "What thin-s, cold affections" (Henry Vaughan, Silex Scirtillans)

parts.words: "What thin-s, cold affections" (Henry Vaughan, Silex Scirtillans)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-gap quotation: the missing plural word completes Vaughan's line in Silex Scintillans

explanation.definitionFit: The noun means throwing out, completing Vaughan's line about thin outpourings of feeling.

clue.text: Othello said he did nought in it

definitions.text: Othello said he did nought in it

parts.words: Othello said he did nought in it
parts.note: Othello claims For nought did I in ... but all in honour, of killing Desdemona

explanation.definitionFit: Othello insists he killed his wife out of honour, not out of loathing.

clue.text: Jeremy Nash, misunderstood novelist

indicators.note: something misunderstood is taken the wrong way, so the name's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Jeremy Nash is an author whom people fail to grasp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misunderstood' rearranges the letters of JEREMY NASH.
explanation.definitionFit: The American-born author of The Ambassadors and The Golden Bowl wrote many novels.

clue.text: Scene of restoration of stable conditions

definitions.text: Scene of restoration of stable conditions

parts.words: Scene of restoration of stable conditions
parts.note: Hercules cleaned King Augeas's filthy stables as one of his labours

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective is from King Augeas, whose stables Hercules cleaned by diverting rivers.

clue.text: He showed the way to win her

definitions.text: He showed the way to win her

parts.words: He showed the way to win her
parts.note: the Irish dramatist's comedy The Inconstant is subtitled The Way to Win Him

explanation.definitionFit: George Farquhar's comedy The Inconstant is subtitled The Way to Win Him; the clue swaps the sex.

clue.text: Shabby sort leads Flashman rogue up to politician

indicators.note: the leads of the three words are their opening letters

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Flashman, the rogue, works his way up to Parliament though dressed shabbily.
explanation.walkthrough: Flashman is the bully of Tom Brown's Schooldays, later the caddish hero of George MacDonald Fraser's novels.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowdy, drably dressed person is a shabby type.

clue.text: One great one immortalized by Grantland Rice

definitions.text: One great one immortalized by Grantland Rice

parts.words: One great one immortalized by Grantland Rice
parts.note: Rice's verse: when the One Great ... comes to mark against your name

explanation.definitionFit: Rice's line pictures God as a recorder of points marking each life, a sports image.

clue.text: One of the golden ones familiar to Keats?

definitions.text: One of the golden ones familiar to Keats?

parts.words: One of the golden ones familiar to Keats
parts.note: Keats's sonnet opens Much have I travelled in the ... of gold

explanation.definitionFit: A kingdom or domain; Keats travelled in the golden ones of literature.

clue.text: Spring spur

parts.note: Howard Spring wrote the novel ... is the Spur, from Milton's Lycidas

explanation.definitionFit: Renown is the spur in Milton's line, borrowed as Howard Spring's novel title.

clue.text: Both fowler and partridge took note of it

definitions.text: Both fowler and partridge took note of it

parts.words: Both fowler and partridge took note of it
parts.note: H. W. Fowler wrote Modern English ... and Eric Partridge wrote ... and ..., both language guides

explanation.definitionFit: Customary handling of words was the subject of Fowler's and Partridge's style guides.

clue.text: Like Lurie's friends or Ewart's love affair

definitions.text: Like Lurie's friends or Ewart's love affair

parts.words: Like Lurie's friends or Ewart's love affair
parts.note: Alison Lurie wrote ... Friends and Gavin Ewart The ... Love Affair

explanation.definitionFit: Both titles describe things existing only in the mind, made up rather than real.

clue.text: "I wouldn't really call it a cushion, is a more common name for it " (Stephen Fry)

definitions.text: "I wouldn't really call it a cushion, is a more common name for it " (Stephen Fry)

parts.words: "I wouldn't really call it a cushion, is a more common name for it " (Stephen Fry)
parts.note: Fry's joke treats a small flat-faced lapdog as a cushion

explanation.definitionFit: The small Chinese lapdog breed is the cushion-like pet Fry jokes about.

clue.text: Henry Reed's instructor was one of parts

definitions.text: Henry Reed's instructor was one of parts

parts.words: Henry Reed's instructor was one of parts
parts.note: Reed's poem Naming of Parts is voiced by a drill instructor naming rifle parts

explanation.definitionFit: The instructor in Reed's poem identifies each rifle part, so he labels them.
